correctness.rationale: The published source supplies the exact three-branch profile with all parameter ranges. Differentiation gives a strictly decreasing first branch, a second branch with one interior maximum and therefore endpoint minima, and a strictly increasing third branch. Exact endpoint comparison shows the golden-ratio junction is strictly below the competing value 10/7. The vertex list at that parameter satisfies the regular-decagon recurrence v_{j+1}=phi v_j-v_{j-1}, proving affine regularity. The bundled verifier rechecks all algebraic identities exactly in Q(sqrt(5)).
risks: The proof treats Mizuguchi's exact profile as an established published premise rather than reproducing its lengthy underlying isosceles-orthogonality calculation.

value.rationale: The source presents a natural complete one-parameter class of decagonal Radon planes, so locating its unique least-James member is a canonical family optimization rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. The minimizer is geometrically distinguished: it is precisely the affine-regular decagon. The exact minimum also coincides with an independently computed Banach--Mazur distance of that same decagon, linking two otherwise different measures of non-Euclidean geometry without asserting a general identity. This identifies which member of the published family is closest to Hilbert behavior as measured by J and supplies a rigid geometric equality case.
risks: The conclusion is family-specific and does not order all Radon planes by James constant.
